INTERNAL RISKS RELATED TO OUR BUSINESS
Our Company has availed secured borrowings from banks and financial institutions, and any
default, delay, or non-compliance with the terms of these loan facilities may lead to enforcement
actions against our charged assets, thereby adversely affecting our operations, financial condition,
and creditworthiness.
Our Company has availed various secured loan facilities from banks and financial institutions to fund our
business requirements, including working capital needs, equipment procurement, and capital expenditure.
In connection with such borrowings, our lenders have created a charge over our movable and other assets,
including certain material handling equipment, through hypothecation or other forms of security interest.
These loan facilities are subject to various covenants, such as timely repayment of principal and interest,
maintenance of specified financial ratios, restrictions on creating additional encumbrances, and other
operational or financial conditions. Any breach of these covenants, delay or default in repayment, or non-
compliance with the terms of the financing agreements may empower the lenders to invoke their rights,

including seizure or restriction of use of essential equipment, freezing of accounts, or initiation of recovery
proceedings. Such enforcement actions could disrupt our operations, impact our ability to meet contractual
obligations to clients, and materially impair our core rental and trading business.
Moreover, our reliance on external borrowings exposes us to financial risks, including increased interest
burdens, reduced cash flows, and lower financial flexibility. Any downgrade in our creditworthiness or a
history of defaults may restrict our ability to raise future debt on favourable terms or at all. Further, adverse
macroeconomic events such as rising interest rates, withdrawal of sanctioned limits, or a systemic liquidity
crisis may affect our access to timely financing and impact business continuity.

Our business is substantially dependent on revenue from the rental of Material Handling Equipment
and Aerial Work Platforms, and any adverse developments affecting demand for such equipment
could materially and adversely affect could materially affect our business, financial condition, results

Our business is substantially dependent on the rental of Material Handling Equipment (MHE). We have
also expanded our offerings to include Aerial Work Platforms (“AWP”) which we provide on a rental basis
to customers across various industries, including manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, and industrial
infrastructure. Rental income constituted 93.72%, 87.66%, 90.46% and 92.45% of our revenue from
operations for the three months period ended June 30, 2026 and for the Fiscal 2026, Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal
2024, respectively. Accordingly, our revenue is substantially dependent on the continued demand for our
MHE and AWP rental services.
Given this revenue concentration, our business, financial condition and results of operations are sensitive
to adverse developments affecting the MHE and AWP rental industry.  Such developments may include,
but are not limited to, changes in regulatory policies, macroeconomic downturns, shifts in government
infrastructure spending, tightening of industrial capital expenditure, disruptions in the supply chain, rising
fuel or equipment costs, increased competition, or rapid technological advancements leading to market
obsolescence of current offerings.
Such events may cause a decline in customer demand, pricing pressures, order cancellations, or delays in
deployment, which could materially affect our ability to maintain or grow revenues and profitability. Our
limited revenue diversification amplifies this risk. Our dependence on MHE and AWP rental sales is also
demonstrated in our Restated Financial Information for the three months period ended June 30, 2026 and

A significant portion of our revenue is derived from repeat business and rental arrangements. Accordingly,
any decline in customer renewal rates, default by major customer, or failure to onboard new customer may
materially impact our cash flows and working capital position. There is no assurance that our past
performance in this segment will continue or that we will be able to sustain or increase its contribution to
our future revenue.
Our revenues are concentrated among certain customers, and the loss of, or a significant reduction
in business from, one or more of our major customers may affect our business and financial
performance and results of operations.
We derive a significant portion of our revenue from a limited number of customers. For the three months
period ended June 30, 2026 and for the Fiscal 2026, Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2024, our top 10 customers
contributed approximately 33.73%, 25.70%, 26.90% and 31.86%, respectively, of our total revenue from
operations. During the same periods, our largest customer contributed approximately 5.89%, 3.33%, 3.97%
and 5.68%, for the three months period ended June 30, 2026, and for the Fiscal 2026, Fiscal 2025 and
Fiscal 2024 respectively, of our total revenue from operations.
Our ability to maintain our revenues and profitability depend, to a certain extent, on our ability to retain
our existing customers and continue to receive business from them. Our customers may reduce, defer or
discontinue their requirements for our MHE and AWP rental and trading services for various reasons,
including changes in their business, operational requirements, capital expenditure plans or business
volumes. Further, our rental arrangements may be terminated prior to their scheduled expiry or may not be
renewed upon expiry, in each case, in accordance with their respective terms.
The loss of, or a material reduction in business from, any of our major customers, or our inability to secure
new customers on comparable commercial terms within a reasonable timeframe, could adversely affect
our revenues and equipment utilisation levels. It may also require us to incur additional costs to redeploy
our equipment or secure new customers.

While we continue to undertake efforts to diversify our customer base and maintain long standing
relationship with existing customers, there can be no assurance that we will be able to reduce our
dependence on any of our major customers. Any such loss or reduction in business could adversely affect
our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows.
Our Company has acquired Material Handling Equipment (“MHE”) from a Promoter Group entity
without executing a formal purchase agreement and e-way bills were not generated in connection
with such transactions. Any non-compliance with applicable GST laws or other regulatory
requirements may adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
During Fiscal 2026, our Company acquired 642 units of MHE from Watrana Traction Company, a
Promoter Group entity. Prior to the acquisition, the aforesaid equipment was already deployed at various
customer sites. Accordingly, the acquisition involved a transfer of ownership of the equipment from
Watrana Traction Company to our Company, without any corresponding physical movement or
transportation of such equipment, as the equipment continued to remain deployed at the respective
customer sites.
No formal purchase agreement was executed in connection with the aforesaid acquisition.
However, the transactions are supported by relevant tax invoices, e-invoices and corporate approvals,
including the Board Resolution dated November 11, 2025, and the Shareholders' Resolution dated
December 4, 2025.
Further, since the aforesaid acquisition involved only a transfer of ownership of the equipment, which was
already deployed at various customer sites, and did not involve any physical movement or transportation
of such equipment, no e-way bills were generated in connection with the said acquisition. While our
Company believes that the aforesaid transactions were undertaken in accordance with applicable laws,
any queries or clarifications sought by the relevant authorities in relation to the documentation or
compliance requirements of such transactions shall be appropriately addressed by our Company. However,
any adverse regulatory determination in relation to such transactions may have an adverse effect on our
business, financial condition and results of operations.
Our reliance on third parties for the maintenance and servicing of our Material Handling Equipment
and AWP fleet may adversely affect our business, results of operations, and financial condition.
Our business operations are heavily reliant on the availability and performance of our fleet of Material
Handling Equipment and AWP, which is rented out to various industrial customers. We do not perform in-
house maintenance or servicing of our fleet but instead depend on third-party service providers for
preventive and corrective maintenance, breakdown support, and overhauls. However, our Company has
not entered into any formal technical service or maintenance agreements with such service providers and
relies on ad-hoc servicing arrangements and our internal technical team for equipment upkeep.
This dependence exposes us to risks related to delays, inefficiencies, or failures by third-party vendors to
carry out timely maintenance, especially during periods of high operational demand. Any such lapse may
result in increased equipment downtime, disruption in client services, non-fulfillment of contractual
obligations, and reputational damage. Furthermore, inconsistencies in service quality or the unavailability
of spare parts may adversely affect the performance and longevity of our fleet.
As our fleet expands or operates across new geographies, the absence of formal maintenance arrangements
may compound operational inefficiencies and impact long-term asset utilization and profitability. Any
inability to find competent alternate service providers on commercially viable terms may further affect our
operations, client satisfaction, and financial condition.
